\label{lemma-local-source-target-implies}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of schemes which is
\'etale local on source-and-target. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{P}$ is \'etale local on the source,
\item $\mathcal{P}$ is \'etale local on the target,
\item $\mathcal{P}$ is stable under postcomposing with \'etale morphisms:
if $f : X \to Y$ has $\mathcal{P}$ and $g : Y \to Z$ is \'etale, then
$g \circ f$ has $\mathcal{P}$, and
\item $\mathcal{P}$ has a permanence property: given $f : X \to Y$ and
$g : Y \to Z$ \'etale such that $g \circ f$ has $\mathcal{P}$, then
$f$ has $\mathcal{P}$.
\end{enumerate}
statement: A property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms is *étale-local on source-and-target* in the stronger sense if (i) it is stable under precomposition with étale maps; (ii) stable under étale base change on the target; and (iii) for each $f:X\to Y$, $\mathcal P(f)$ is equivalent to the existence, for every $x\in X$, of a commutative diagram $U\xrightarrow hV$, $U\xrightarrow aX$, $V\xrightarrow bY$ with $a,b$ étale near a point $u$ above $x$ and $h$ having $\mathcal P$. This is stronger than merely asking for separate source- and target-locality. Every such $\mathcal P$ is separately étale-local on the source and separately étale-local on the target. Moreover, it is stable under postcomposition with étale morphisms: if $f:X\to Y$ has $\mathcal P$ and $g:Y\to Z$ is étale, then $g\circ f$ has $\mathcal P$. Conversely, if $g$ is étale and $g\circ f$ has $\mathcal P$, then $f$ has $\mathcal P$.
hypotheses: P satisfies the strong étale-local-on-source-and-target criterion.
conclusions: Separate source and target locality and the two étale-postcomposition implications follow.

\label{lemma-local-source-target-global-implies-local}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of schemes
which is \'etale local on the source-and-target.
Consider the property $\mathcal{Q}$ of
morphisms of germs defined by the rule
$$
\mathcal{Q}((X, x) \to (S, s))
\Leftrightarrow
\text{there exists a representative }U \to S
\text{ which has }\mathcal{P}
$$
Then $\mathcal{Q}$ is \'etale local on the source-and-target as in
Definition \ref{definition-local-source-target-at-point}.

\label{lemma-Zariski-refinement-coverings-equivalence}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}_{i \in I}$, and
$\mathcal{V} = \{V_j \to S\}_{j \in J}$,
be families of morphisms with target $S$.
Let $\alpha : I \to J$, $\text{id} : S \to S$ and
$g_i : U_i \to V_{\alpha(i)}$ be a morphism of families
of maps with fixed target, see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-morphism-coverings}.
Assume that for each $j \in J$ the family
$\{g_i : U_i \to V_j\}_{\alpha(i) = j}$ is a Zariski covering (see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-zariski-covering})
of $V_j$. Then the pullback functor
$$
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{V}
\longrightarrow
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{U}
$$
of Lemma \ref{lemma-pullback-family} is an equivalence of categories.
In particular, the category of schemes over $S$
is equivalent to the category
of descent data relative to any Zariski covering of $S$.
statement: For a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S\}$, let $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ be the category of families of $U_i$-schemes $V_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_SU_j\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i\times_SV_j$ over $U_i\times_SU_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A morphism of families $(\alpha,g_i):\mathcal U\to\mathcal V=\{V_j\to S\}$ comprises a function $\alpha:I\to J$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ over $S$; it induces a pullback functor $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$. Suppose for every $j\in J$ the subfamily $\{g_i:U_i\to V_j\mid\alpha(i)=j\}$ is a Zariski open covering of $V_j$. Then pullback $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ is an equivalence of categories, not just fully faithful. In particular, if $\{U_i\to S\}$ is any Zariski open covering, $\operatorname{Sch}/S$ is equivalent to the category of scheme descent data for this cover, via ordinary gluing.
hypotheses: The refinement is, on each V_j, a Zariski open covering.
conclusions: The induced pullback is an equivalence; schemes descend effectively along Zariski covers.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-refine-coverings-fully-faithful}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to S\}_{i \in I}$, and
$\mathcal{V} = \{V_j \to S\}_{j \in J}$,
be fpqc-coverings of $S$.
If $\mathcal{U}$ is a refinement of $\mathcal{V}$,
then the pullback functor
$$
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{V}
\longrightarrow
\text{descent data relative to }
\mathcal{U}
$$
is fully faithful.
In particular, the category of schemes over $S$
is identified with a full subcategory of the category
of descent data relative to any fpqc-covering of $S$.
statement: For a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to S\}$, let $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ be the category of families of $U_i$-schemes $V_i$ together with isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:V_i\times_SU_j\xrightarrow{\sim}U_i\times_SV_j$ over $U_i\times_SU_j$ satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps. A morphism of families $(\alpha,g_i):\mathcal U\to\mathcal V=\{V_j\to S\}$ comprises a function $\alpha:I\to J$ and maps $g_i:U_i\to V_{\alpha(i)}$ over $S$; it induces a pullback functor $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$. Let $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal V$ both be fpqc coverings of $S$, and suppose $\mathcal U$ refines $\mathcal V$. Then the induced pullback $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal V)\to\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ is fully faithful. Consequently, for any fpqc covering $\mathcal U$ of $S$, the category $\operatorname{Sch}/S$ embeds fully faithfully into $\mathrm{DD}(\mathcal U)$ through canonical descent data. No assertion that this embedding is essentially surjective for all schemes is made.
hypotheses: Both covers fpqc and U refines V.
conclusions: Refinement pullback is fully faithful, and schemes over S embed fully faithfully into descent data on an fpqc cover.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-effective-for-fpqc-is-local-upstairs}
Let $X \to S$ be a surjective, quasi-compact, flat morphism of
schemes. Let $(V, \varphi)$ be a descent datum relative to $X/S$.
Suppose that for all $v \in V$ there exists an open subscheme
$v \in W \subset V$ such that $\varphi(W \times_S X) \subset X \times_S W$
and such that the descent datum $(W, \varphi|_{W \times_S X})$
is effective. Then $(V, \varphi)$ is effective.
statement: Fix $p:X\to S$. Write $\mathrm{DD}(X/S)$ for the category of descent data for schemes along $X\to S$. An object is a scheme $V\to X$ and an isomorphism $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim} X\times_SV$ over $X\times_SX$ satisfying the cocycle identity on $X\times_SX\times_SX$. Morphisms are $X$-morphisms compatible with these isomorphisms. For a morphism $f:X'\to X$ over $S$, pullback is the functor $f^*:\mathrm{DD}(X/S)\to\mathrm{DD}(X'/S)$ taking $V$ to $V\times_X X'$ and $\varphi$ to its pullback along $f\times_Sf$. Let $p:X\to S$ be surjective, flat, and quasi-compact. Let $(V\to X,\varphi)$ be a descent datum relative to $X/S$. Say the datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical pullback $(X\times_SU,\mathrm{can})$ of some scheme $U\to S$. Suppose every $v\in V$ has an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq V$ such that (i) the descent isomorphism preserves that open, $\varphi(W\times_SX)\subseteq X\times_SW$, so the restriction $\varphi|_{W\times_SX}$ defines descent data on $W$, and (ii) this restricted datum is effective. Then $(V,\varphi)$ itself is effective, by descending overlaps and gluing the resulting $S$-schemes.
hypotheses: X→S is an fpqc singleton cover; V with descent datum admits compatible open effective neighbourhoods covering V.
conclusions: The global descent datum is effective.
